title: Fluid Mechanics
description: A one-semester engineering Fluid Mechanics course following calculus, physics, and statics/dynamics. It balances physical intuition, conservation-law modeling, engineering calculations, and laboratory interpretation.

resources.title: Fluid Mechanics

resources.description: Cengel and Cimbala text with accessible applications and visuals.

resources.title: Engineering Fluid Mechanics
resources.description: Crowe text for applied fluids, measurements, and engineering systems.

resources.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
resources.description: Foundational fluid concepts and problem solving.

resources.title: MIT OCW Fluid Dynamics
resources.description: MIT course covering hydrostatics, control volumes, viscous flow, and applications.

resources.title: Engineering LibreTexts - Fluid Mechanics
resources.description: Open fluid mechanics text and examples.

resources.title: LearnChemE Fluid Mechanics
resources.description: Fluid mechanics screencasts for balances, pressure, pipes, and pumps.

resources.title: NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide to Aerodynamics

resources.title: NPTEL Fluid Mechanics

topics.title: Course Orientation, Fluid Properties, and Continuum Modeling
topics.description: This opening unit establishes what makes a fluid different from a solid and how engineers model fluid behavior. Students learn the properties, units, and assumptions used throughout the course.

videos.title: What Is a Fluid? Course Overview
videos.annotation: Start here — sets up the whole course.

children.title: Fluids and the Continuum Assumption
children.description: Students learn when matter can be treated as a continuous field rather than individual molecules.

videos.title: System, Control Mass, and Control Volume

children.title: System, control mass, and control volume
Fluid Properties
children.description: Fluid properties connect material behavior to forces, flow, and energy loss.

children.title: Density, specific weight, and specific gravity
Surface tension, vapor pressure, and compressibility
Engineering Modeling and Units
children.description: A consistent modeling workflow keeps fluid calculations physically meaningful.

videos.title: SI vs US Customary Units in Fluids

topics.title: Fluid Statics, Pressure Variation, and Pressure Measurement
topics.description: Fluid statics studies fluids at rest. This unit teaches how pressure varies with depth and how engineers measure pressure reliably.

children.title: Pressure Concepts
children.description: Students learn pressure as a normal stress and distinguish common reference scales.

videos.title: Absolute vs Gauge vs Vacuum Pressure

children.title: Hydrostatic Pressure Variation
children.description: Students derive and apply the relationship between pressure and elevation.

children.title: Pressure Measurement
children.description: Students learn how devices translate pressure differences into measurable quantities.

topics.title: Hydrostatic Forces, Buoyancy, and Stability
topics.description: This unit applies pressure fields to submerged and floating bodies. Students learn how distributed pressure creates resultant forces and moments.

children.title: Forces on Plane and Curved Surfaces
children.description: Students reduce distributed hydrostatic pressure to useful resultants.

videos.title: Hydrostatic Force on a Plane Surface

children.title: Buoyancy
children.description: Archimedes' principle explains the upward force on immersed objects.

children.title: Stability of Floating and Submerged Bodies
children.description: Students learn why some bodies return to equilibrium while others overturn.

children.title: Center of gravity and center of buoyancy

topics.title: Fluid Kinematics and Flow Description
topics.description: Kinematics describes fluid motion without yet asking what forces cause it. Students learn to describe velocity fields, flow patterns, and local deformation.

children.title: Flow Classification
children.description: Students learn standard ways to characterize fluid motion.

videos.title: Steady vs Unsteady, Uniform vs Nonuniform

children.title: Velocity Fields and Streamlines
children.description: Velocity fields help students visualize how fluid particles move.

children.title: Rotation and Deformation
children.description: Students get an introductory view of how fluid elements translate, rotate, and strain.

topics.title: Bernoulli Equation and Mechanical Energy Concepts
topics.description: Bernoulli's equation connects pressure, velocity, and elevation along a flow. Students learn both its power and its limitations.

children.title: Derivation and Assumptions
children.description: Students learn when Bernoulli is valid rather than using it as a universal formula.

children.title: Bernoulli Applications
children.description: Students apply the equation to common devices and flow situations.

children.title: Energy Interpretation
children.description: Students connect Bernoulli terms to mechanical energy per unit weight.

children.title: When losses and machines must be included

topics.title: Control-Volume Conservation of Mass
topics.description: Mass conservation is the first universal balance law of fluid mechanics. Students learn to analyze flow through devices and networks using control volumes.

children.title: Control Volume Framework
children.description: Students learn to draw boundaries around fluid systems and track what crosses them.

children.title: Continuity Equation
children.description: The continuity equation relates density, area, and velocity.

children.title: Applications
children.description: Students use mass conservation in practical flow systems.

topics.title: Control-Volume Momentum and Force Analysis
topics.description: Momentum conservation connects fluid motion to forces on pipes, vanes, jets, and devices. This unit is where flow creates mechanical loads.

children.title: Linear Momentum Equation
children.description: Students learn how momentum flux and external forces balance.

children.title: Momentum Applications
children.description: Students calculate forces produced by changing flow direction or speed.

videos.title: Force on Pipe Bends and Reducers

children.title: Angular Momentum
children.description: Angular momentum provides the foundation for turbomachinery analysis.

topics.title: Energy Equation, Head Losses, and Hydraulic Grade Lines
topics.description: The mechanical energy equation extends Bernoulli to real systems with losses, pumps, and turbines. Students learn to visualize energy changes along a flow path.

videos.title: The Extended Energy Equation
videos.thumbnailQuery: energy equation head loss pump turbine

children.title: Mechanical Energy Equation
children.description: Students account for machines and irreversible losses.

children.title: Grade Lines
children.description: Hydraulic and energy grade lines make pressure and energy behavior visible.

videos.title: Hydraulic and Energy Grade Lines
videos.thumbnailQuery: hydraulic grade line energy grade line

children.title: System Analysis
children.description: Students apply the equation to realistic fluid systems.

topics.title: Dimensional Analysis, Similitude, and Model Testing
topics.description: Dimensional analysis reduces complex flow problems to meaningful nondimensional groups. It also lets engineers test scaled models and transfer results to full-size systems.

children.title: Dimensions and Buckingham Pi
children.description: Students learn how variables combine into dimensionless parameters.

videos.title: The Buckingham Pi Theorem, Step by Step

children.title: Important Dimensionless Numbers
children.description: Dimensionless numbers compare competing physical effects.

children.title: Reynolds, Froude, Euler, Mach, and Weber numbers
Similitude and Scaling
children.description: Students learn how model tests represent prototypes.

topics.title: Internal Flow: Laminar and Turbulent Pipe Flow
topics.description: Internal flow focuses on fluids confined by walls. Students learn how viscosity, turbulence, and roughness determine pressure loss.

videos.title: Pipe Flow: Laminar to Turbulent
videos.thumbnailQuery: pipe flow laminar turbulent velocity profile

children.title: Fully Developed Pipe Flow
children.description: Students learn the structure of laminar and turbulent velocity profiles.

children.title: Reynolds Number and Flow Regimes
children.description: Reynolds number predicts whether viscous or inertial behavior dominates.

children.title: Friction Losses
children.description: Students quantify pressure drop in pipes.

topics.title: Pipe Systems, Pumps, Turbines, and Flow Measurement
topics.description: This unit turns pipe-flow fundamentals into engineering-system analysis. Students learn how components interact and how flow is measured and moved.

children.title: Pipe Networks and Minor Losses
children.description: Students analyze systems with fittings, branches, and multiple pipes.

children.title: Pumps and Turbines
children.description: Students learn how machines add or remove energy from fluids.

videos.title: Pump Curves and Operating Point
videos.thumbnailQuery: pump curve system curve operating point

children.title: Flow Measurement
children.description: Students compare common measurement techniques and their limitations.

topics.title: External Flow, Drag, Lift, and Boundary Layers
topics.description: External flow studies fluid moving around bodies. Students learn how viscous boundary layers create drag, separation, and lift-related effects.

videos.title: Boundary Layers, Drag and Lift Overview

children.title: Boundary Layer Fundamentals
children.description: Students learn how no-slip behavior creates a thin viscous region near surfaces.

videos.title: The No-Slip Condition & Boundary Layers
videos.thumbnailQuery: boundary layer no slip velocity profile

children.title: Drag
children.description: Students learn how shape, skin friction, and separation determine resistance.

children.title: Lift and Flow Around Bodies
children.description: Students gain a foundational view of lift and fluid forces on engineering shapes.

topics.title: Open-Channel Flow and Introductory Compressible Flow
topics.description: This unit introduces two important regimes beyond closed-pipe incompressible flow: free-surface hydraulics and flows where density changes matter.

videos.title: Open-Channel and Compressible Flow Intro
videos.thumbnailQuery: open channel free surface compressible flow

children.title: Open-Channel Flow Concepts
children.description: Students learn how gravity and free surfaces shape channel flow.

children.title: Uniform and Rapidly Varied Flow
children.description: Students survey common hydraulic calculations and transitions.

videos.title: Manning's Equation and the Hydraulic Jump

children.title: Compressible Flow Introduction
children.description: Students learn when gas density changes can no longer be ignored.

videos.title: Mach Number and the Speed of Sound
videos.thumbnailQuery: mach number speed of sound shock

topics.title: Integrated Fluid Mechanics Laboratory and Applications
topics.description: The final unit consolidates the course through measurement, uncertainty, and cross-disciplinary applications. Students practice explaining not only what the equations predict, but whether the result is credible.

videos.title: From Theory to Lab: Putting It Together

children.title: Experimental Methods and Data Quality
children.description: Students learn how fluid quantities are measured and how uncertainty affects conclusions.

children.title: Integrated Engineering Applications
children.description: Students connect core methods to real systems.

videos.title: Fluids in Aerospace and Biomedical Systems

children.title: Model Validation and Communication
children.description: Students learn to present a fluid analysis as an engineering argument.

children.title: Comparison of theory, experiment, and simulation
